- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-0.5) and forecast is below recent low, avoid excessive downward correction — allow slight lagged rebound.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, cap the overshoot by reducing peak by 5–10% to prevent overcorrection.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently 2–3σ above or below recent 10-day average, adjust toward historical mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overfitting to recent 1–2 day sentiment — use 3–5 day sentiment average for smoothing.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, reduce forecast slope — don’t assume momentum continues.  
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >1.5σ, apply downward correction proportional to sentiment decay.
